title: The Hodge Conjecture
description: One of the seven Millennium Prize Problems. Every Hodge class on a projective variety is a rational combination of algebraic cycle classes.

meta.author: W.V.D. Hodge (1950)
meta.assumptions: 100 axiom declarations encoding Hodge structures, Chern classes and K-theory (chern_class_exists, chern_character_ring_hom, Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch), categorical operations (Tate twists, duals, tensor products), algebraic correspondences, known cases (Lefschetz 1,1, abelian varieties, K3, Fermat, flag varieties, hyperkähler), counterexamples (Atiyah-Hirzebruch, Voisin, Totaro), related conjectures (Standard, Mumford-Tate, Tate, Generalized Hodge), and structural results (Hard Lefschetz, polarizations, intermediate Jacobians, motives, p-adic Hodge theory). 433 theorems/definitions including Variational Hodge Conjecture framework. The Hodge Conjecture itself remains open.

overview.historicalContext:
The Hodge Conjecture was proposed by Sir William Vallance Douglas Hodge at the 1950 International Congress of Mathematicians in Cambridge. Hodge developed his theory of harmonic integrals in the 1930s–1940s, building on Solomon Lefschetz's 1924 theorem that every (1,1) integral Hodge class is algebraic (the Lefschetz theorem on (1,1) classes). Hodge conjectured this should extend to all codimensions p.

For over 70 years the conjecture has resisted resolution. Key milestones: Atiyah–Hirzebruch (1962) disproved the integral version using topological K-theory and Steenrod operations, showing rational coefficients are essential. Grothendieck (1968) proposed his Standard Conjectures, which would imply the Hodge Conjecture as a corollary; they also remain open. Deligne proved the Weil conjectures (1974), which are related but distinct. Voisin (2002) proved the conjecture fails for compact Kähler manifolds that are not projective, confirming projectivity is an essential hypothesis.

In 2000, the Clay Mathematics Institute designated the Hodge Conjecture as one of seven Millennium Prize Problems with a $1,000,000 prize. The only proven cases are: divisors on any variety (Lefschetz (1,1)), curves, surfaces, and special abelian varieties (Deligne, Hazama). The conjecture stands as one of the deepest open questions in mathematics.
overview.problemStatement:
**Conjecture:** On a smooth projective variety X over C, every Hodge class is a rational linear combination of algebraic cycle classes.

Formally: H^{p,p}(X) intersect H^{2p}(X,Q) equals the Q-span of algebraic subvariety classes.
overview.proofStrategy:
This file provides:
1. Abstract Hodge structures with complexification maps and injectivity
2. Hodge filtration (decreasing filtration F^p) and Hodge numbers h^{p,q}
3. Hodge symmetry h^{p,q} = h^{q,p} proved from conjugation axiom
4. Integral Hodge conjecture and proof that rational follows from integral
5. Formal counterexample axioms (Atiyah-Hirzebruch, Voisin)
6. Proven cases (Lefschetz theorem, curves, surfaces)
7. Equivalent formulations (Standard Conjectures, Mumford-Tate)
8. Morphisms of Hodge structures with functoriality on Hodge/algebraic classes
9. Polarizations with proved symmetry/antisymmetry for even/odd weight
10. Mixed Hodge structures with pure-to-mixed embedding
keyInsights: The conjecture is OPEN - one of the Millennium Prize Problems
The Lefschetz (1,1) theorem is the proven case for divisors
Voisin showed it fails for Kahler manifolds (projectivity essential)
Atiyah-Hirzebruch showed integral coefficients fail (rational essential)
Hodge symmetry h^{p,q} = h^{q,p} is proved from the conjugation axiom
The complexification map connects rational classes to complex decomposition

sections.title: Hodge Structures with Complexification
sections.summary: Pure Hodge structures with complexification map ι : V_ℚ →ₗ[ℚ] V_ℂ and Hodge components V^{p,q}.

sections.title: Hodge Decomposition and Numbers
sections.summary: Hodge conjugation symmetry axiom, Hodge numbers h^{p,q}, and proved Hodge symmetry h^{p,q} = h^{q,p}.

sections.title: Hodge Filtration
sections.summary: Decreasing filtration F^p on V_ℂ with F^0 = V_ℂ and F^{k+1} = 0.

sections.title: Hodge Classes
sections.summary: Hodge classes defined as rational classes whose complexification lies in V^{p,p}.

sections.title: The Conjecture
sections.summary: Formal statement of the Hodge Conjecture.

sections.title: Counterexamples
sections.summary: Integral Hodge conjecture, Atiyah-Hirzebruch failure, Voisin Kähler counterexample, and proof that rational follows from integral.

sections.title: Morphisms of Hodge Structures
sections.summary: Morphisms with rational and complex components, identity, composition, functoriality on Hodge classes and algebraic classes.

sections.title: Sub-Hodge Structures
sections.summary: Sub-Hodge structures, full and zero instances, kernel of a morphism is a sub-Hodge structure.

sections.title: Polarizations
sections.summary: Polarized Hodge structures with proved symmetry for even weight and antisymmetry for odd weight.

sections.title: Mixed Hodge Structures
sections.summary: Mixed Hodge structures with weight filtration, Deligne's theorem, and pure-to-mixed embedding.

conclusion.summary: The Hodge Conjecture remains open. This formalization provides a rigorous mathematical framework including complexification maps, Hodge filtrations, Hodge numbers with symmetry properties, and formal counterexample statements.
conclusion.implications: The conjecture is fundamental to algebraic geometry and topology. Its resolution would have profound implications for our understanding of algebraic varieties, motives, and the relationship between topology and algebra.
openQuestions: What is the relationship to motives and Grothendieck's Standard Conjectures?
Can the Lefschetz approach extend to higher codimension?
What role does the Hodge filtration play in finding algebraic cycles?
